data.title: DETERRENCE: THREE REVOLUTIONS IN ONE WORD
data.source: Brodie, *The Absolute Weapon* (1946); Schelling, *Arms and Influence* (1966)

events.title: Atomic
events.definition: Nuclear weapons make war between great powers rationally impossible. Mutual destruction as the deterrent — punishment without defense.

events.title: Extended
events.definition: NATO extends nuclear deterrence to conventional attack. The threat must be credible; credibility becomes the central analytical problem.
events.keyPassage: "The art of commitment is to burn your bridges behind you." — Schelling

events.title: Conventional
events.definition: NATO shifts to AirLand Battle doctrine. Conventional deterrence returns as the primary layer; nuclear becomes last resort.

events.title: Hybrid
events.definition: Russia's 'little green men' expose deterrence gaps below the NATO Article 5 threshold. Deterrence must now cover gray-zone operations.
